# OA v0.7.19

**Status:** Released public development preview

**Released:** 2026-08-26

**Source:** [`v0.7.19`](https://github.com/realminc/oa/releases/tag/v0.7.19)

## Summary

OA v0.7.19 publishes the private `v0.7.1` foundation checkpoint. Maintained
product code now uses bounded OA contracts for containers, ownership,
synchronization, time, filesystem, command-line parsing, Unicode, and platform
I/O while preserving the existing engine, operation, SDK, and package model.

This milestone does not claim linked-binary independence from `libstdc++` or
`libc++`. Remaining third-party, compiler, platform, and fault-qualification
work is explicit under Known limitations.

## Highlights

- OA-owned generated C++ contains zero hosted-library symbols, headers,
  exception tokens, and RTTI tokens under the checked audit.
- Native `oa::Cli<TConfig>`, `oa::CmdCli`, and `oa::OptCli` replace CLI11 and
  fmt; utf8proc 2.11.3 is vendored as an exact private C dependency.
- Sort reaches parity and hash insertion/lookup outperform the host
  implementation on the recorded workload; shared ownership remains slower.
- The dependency ratchet prevents new hosted-library use above the accepted
  owned, public, foundation, generated, vendored, and closure ceilings.

## Added

- Allocation, lifetime, iteration, value composition, ownership,
  synchronization, thread, time, path, filesystem, CLI, and platform-adapter
  contracts under the direct `oa` vocabulary.
- Collision, tombstone, rehash, lifetime, concurrent release, CLI, filesystem,
  serialization, and benchmark verification.
- Public [foundation benchmark](../benchmarks/oaStd.md) evidence with exact
  protocol, spread, reproduction commands, and non-claims.

## Improved

- `HashMap` uses cache-dense open addressing with explicit empty and tombstone
  states, immutable iterator keys, and a single successful-lookup slot scan.
- Sorting uses bounded introsort with median-of-three partitioning,
  small-range insertion sort, and a heapsort depth limit.
- Product queues, histories, log synchronization, capture rings, validation
  state, and runtime services use OA-owned storage and synchronization.
- The root README now uses the exact runnable C++ and Python SDK matrix examples
  and leaves release inventories in versioned release notes.

## Fixed

- CLI command and option handles retain stable addresses after later entries
  are added; explicitly empty values remain distinct from missing values; help
  is a successful application outcome.
- Python filesystem and media bindings construct OA paths and string views
  explicitly after hosted conversion constructors were removed.
- Fail-fast rejection tests no longer expect hosted exceptions.
- Distributed split-batch verification independently proves gradient parity
  and the first-step AdamW response at the accepted FP32 tolerance.

## Removed

- CLI11 and fmt package, include, link, and installed-header dependencies.
- Ordinary hosted container, string, ownership, synchronization, clock,
  filesystem, stream, and exception use from migrated OA-owned product paths.
- Public hosted-filesystem conversions, the redundant `StdFilesystem` facade,
  and the obsolete ALM animation from the root README assets.

## Compatibility and migration

- OA remains pre-1.0. Rebuild C++ and Python consumers for this release.
- OA-owned code uses `oa::Vec`, `oa::String`, `oa::SharedPtr`, `oa::sort`, and
  `oa::move`; no `oa::std`, `oastd`, or `OaStd*` compatibility layer exists.
- CLI consumers use `oa::Cli<TConfig>`, `oa::CmdCli`, and `oa::OptCli` rather
  than CLI11 types.
- Public hosted-filesystem conversion constructors were removed. Construct an
  `oa::Path` or `oa::StringView` explicitly at an external boundary.
- `std::initializer_list` remains the admitted brace-construction language
  bridge; module-specific list wrappers are not introduced.
- Model, checkpoint, execution-plan, Python ABI, and C++ ABI compatibility are
  not promised across pre-1.0 versions.

## Performance

The accepted fixed-host comparison used Clang 22.1.8, glibc 2.44, CPU 2
affinity, five warmups, 21 alternating samples, and seven fresh processes. All
checksums passed. Ratios below 1.0 favor OA.

| Workload | OA/host median | Seven-process range |
|---|---:|---:|
| Algorithm sort | 0.994x | 0.980–1.035x |
| `HashMap` insertion | 0.459x | 0.446–0.468x |
| `HashMap` successful find | 0.871x | 0.793–0.906x |
| `SharedPtr` make/release | 1.579x | 1.271–1.610x |
| `SharedPtr` copy/release | 1.919x | 1.720–2.016x |

The [foundation benchmark](../benchmarks/oaStd.md) owns absolute medians,
before/after ratios, exact reproduction commands, and the evidence boundary.

## Verification

| Gate | Result | Evidence scope |
|---|---|---|
| Foundation | Pass | 209 focused correctness tests on the private source checkpoint |
| Release | Pass | 153/153 CTest targets; zero failures and zero skips |
| ASAN/LSAN | Pass | 153/153 CTest targets |
| UBSAN | Pass | 153/153 CTest targets |
| Python | Pass | host 36, crypto-host 8, GPU 94, crypto-GPU 10; skips forbidden |
| Generation/docs | Pass | generated-source, example, documentation, architecture, asset, and dependency-ratchet checks |
| Package/install | Pass | clean staged install and external `find_package(oa 0.7.19 EXACT)` consumer |
| Physical GPU | No new route claim | Intel Iris Xe executes the unchanged runtime paths used by focused examples and Python GPU profiles |

The tagged GitHub workflow owns hosted CPU-Vulkan, sanitizer, package, wheel,
PyPI, release-asset, and checksum evidence. A pending or failed hosted job is
not converted into a pass by this source note.

## Known limitations

- The installed public-header closure retains the admitted
  `std::initializer_list` language bridge and yaml-cpp adapter.
- VMA and selected private dependencies remain in the complete hosted-library
  and link audit. Binary independence is not shipped.
- Shared ownership is slower than the host implementation in the measured
  make/copy/release workloads.
- Linux x86-64 is the runtime-qualified foundation platform. Android, Windows,
  Apple, additional compilers, race/fuzz/fault injection, and linked-binary
  independence remain unverified.
- Vulkan Video and GPU routes remain capability, device, driver, and
  queue-topology dependent and fail closed when unavailable.

## Upgrade

Rebuild native consumers and Python wheels, replace CLI11-facing code with the
native OA CLI surface, construct OA path/text values explicitly at external
boundaries, regenerate checked source inventories, and discard stale build,
package, execution-plan, and pre-1.0 binary caches.
